title: The Last Copy of a Book
fact_notes: 架空の教材例。実在の書籍・歴史資料・人物・制度・法令についての記述ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: In an imagined town, a small independent bookshop is preparing to close after many years of operation, and its owner invites local residents to purchase items from its remaining collection.
sentences.ja: 架空の町で長年営業した小規模独立書店が閉店準備をし、所有者は残った蔵書を購入するよう住民を招く。

sentences.en: One of the books attracts considerable attention because it contains handwritten comments left by several people who worked together on a community project many decades earlier.
sentences.ja: 数十年前に地域活動を共同で行った複数人の手書きコメントが入っているため、一冊がかなり注目を集める。

sentences.en: A collector offers to purchase the book for a personal collection, while a local reading group asks whether it could instead be made available to people interested in the town's history.
sentences.ja: 収集家が個人蔵書用に購入を申し出る一方、地元読書会は町の歴史に関心がある人々に利用可能にできないか尋ねる。

sentences.en: The owner appreciates both offers but wonders whether responsibility for the future of the book should be determined exclusively by finding the person willing to pay the highest price.
sentences.ja: 所有者は両申し出をありがたく思うが、本の将来への責任を最高額を払う人を見つけることだけで決めるべきか疑問に思う。

sentences.en: The collector explains that acquiring unusual books involves more than obtaining objects that can be displayed or sold, since maintaining a collection may require knowledge, careful storage, and considerable expenditure.
sentences.ja: 珍しい本の入手は展示・販売できる物を得る以上を伴うと収集家は説明する。蔵書維持には知識、慎重な保管、かなりの支出が必要な場合があるからだ。

sentences.en: Members of the reading group acknowledge that transferring a book to an organization describing itself as a public resource would not necessarily guarantee that the object would receive appropriate care.
sentences.ja: 公共資源と称する団体への移管が物の適切な保護を保証するとは限らないと読書会の会員は認める。

sentences.en: They also recognize that making an original object available for frequent handling might conflict with the objective of preserving it for people who will become interested in it many years later.
sentences.ja: 原物を頻繁に扱えるようにすることは何年も後に関心を持つ人々のため保存する目的と衝突し得るとも認識する。

sentences.en: The discussion consequently distinguishes ownership of the book from the responsibilities and opportunities associated with its preservation and use.
sentences.ja: そこで本の所有と保存・利用に伴う責任や機会を区別する。

sentences.en: Rather than assuming that only one of the interested parties can contribute to the book's future, the owner invites them to consider several possible arrangements.
sentences.ja: 本の将来に貢献できるのは関係者の一方だけと想定せず、複数の仕組みを考えるよう所有者は招く。

sentences.en: The collector might agree to make the item available for occasional supervised examination, provided that the practical conditions required for protecting it can be established.
sentences.ja: 保護に必要な実務条件が整えば収集家は時折監督下での閲覧を可能にすることに同意するかもしれない。

sentences.en: Alternatively, the reading group could investigate whether a suitable reproduction might allow people to study the handwritten material without requiring the original book to travel between different locations.
sentences.ja: 別案として原本が異なる場所間を移動する必要なく手書き資料を研究できる適切な複製物が作れるか読書会は調べられる。

sentences.en: They acknowledge that such possibilities would require consideration of the rights and expectations associated with reproducing the material, rather than assuming that physical possession automatically authorizes every possible use.
sentences.ja: そのような可能性は物理的所有が全用途を自動的に許可すると想定せず複製に伴う権利と期待を考慮する必要があると認める。

sentences.en: The fictional participants also consider whether their proposed arrangements could remain meaningful if the current owner of the book eventually decided to transfer it to another person.
sentences.ja: 現在所有者がいつか他者へ移すと決めても提案が意味を保てるか架空参加者は考える。

sentences.en: A promise concerning future access may be difficult to evaluate if the conditions under which that promise can be maintained have never been discussed.
sentences.ja: 約束維持の条件が議論されていなければ将来利用の約束を評価しにくい場合がある。

sentences.en: The group therefore identifies responsibilities that would need to be understood and accepted before treating an informal expression of goodwill as a dependable long-term arrangement.
sentences.ja: そこで非公式の善意表明を信頼できる長期的仕組みと扱う前に理解・受容される必要がある責任を特定する。

sentences.en: The example does not establish the legal obligations of book owners or the requirements for reproducing actual historical documents; it explores competing ethical considerations in an imagined situation.
sentences.ja: 例は本所有者の法的義務や実歴史文書複製の要件を確立するのでなく架空状況の競合する倫理的考慮事項を探る。

sentences.en: Possessing an object and making its significance available to other people are different activities, although they can sometimes support each other through carefully considered arrangements.
sentences.ja: 物を所有することと他者がその意義に触れられるようにすることは異なる活動だが慎重に考えられた仕組みで互いを支える場合がある。

sentences.en: A meaningful public purpose does not by itself eliminate the practical costs of caring for an object or justify ignoring the interests of the people who contribute to its preservation.
sentences.ja: 意味ある公共目的だけで物の保護費用がなくなるわけでも保存に貢献する人々の利益を無視することが正当化されるわけでもない。

sentences.en: Responsible decisions therefore require attention to the relationships between access, preservation, and the commitments that people are actually able to sustain.
sentences.ja: 責任ある判断にはアクセス、保存、人々が実際に維持できる約束の関係への注意が必要だ。

sentences.en: For the last copy of the book, the question of who should own it becomes inseparable from the question of what opportunities its future custodians might reasonably provide.
sentences.ja: 最後の一冊について誰が所有すべきかという問いは将来の管理者がどんな機会を合理的に提供できるかという問いと切り離せなくなる。

questions.prompt: Why does the book attract considerable attention?
options: It is the only book the owner is legally permitted to sell.
It contains handwritten comments connected to an earlier community project.
It provides a verified history of every resident.
It is the most expensive new publication in the town.
questions.explanation_ja: 地域活動の手書き記録。

questions.prompt: What does the owner question about the highest offer?
options: Whether every collector intends to sell books immediately.
Whether the book has any physical value.
Whether price alone should determine responsibility for the book's future.
Whether the reading group can read handwritten comments.
questions.explanation_ja: 価格だけで将来を決めるか。

questions.prompt: Why is transfer to a public organization not necessarily sufficient?
options: Public access does not automatically guarantee appropriate preservation.
Every public institution prohibits reading.
Only private collectors have relevant knowledge.
The book becomes historically meaningless when transferred.
questions.explanation_ja: 公開と保存は別の課題。

options: Buying and selling every new book.
Collecting and reading modern novels.
Displaying and pricing ordinary merchandise.
Frequent handling and long-term preservation.

questions.prompt: What arrangement involving the collector is suggested?
options: Unrestricted lending without any protection.
Immediate disposal of the book.
Occasional supervised examination under suitable conditions.
A guarantee that no one may examine it.
It automatically transfers every reproduction right.
It could expand opportunities for study without moving the original.
It demonstrates that the original no longer matters.
It makes preservation of the original impossible.

questions.prompt: What makes a future access promise uncertain?
options: Only the first owner can make any promise.
Every future owner will act identically.
Informal promises are always legally binding.
The conditions necessary to maintain the promise may be undefined.

questions.prompt: What does the example not establish?
options: Legal obligations and actual document reproduction requirements.
The existence of possible ethical trade-offs.
The need to consider practical conditions.
The possibility of different arrangements.
People who determine the price of every item.
People responsible for looking after something.
Visitors who have no responsibility for preservation.
Writers who created a historical document.

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the argument?
options: The highest price always identifies the best custodian.
Public ownership necessarily guarantees preservation.
Decisions about ownership should consider sustainable preservation, access, and responsibilities.
Every historical object must be handled without restrictions.
questions.explanation_ja: 所有・保存・アクセスの関係。

paraphrases.source: The owner appreciates both offers but wonders whether responsibility for the future of the book should be determined exclusively by finding the person willing to pay the highest price.
paraphrases.rewrite: The owner considers whether the highest bid alone should decide the book's future.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 価格による判断を問う。

paraphrases.source: They also recognize that making an original object available for frequent handling might conflict with the objective of preserving it for people who will become interested in it many years later.
paraphrases.rewrite: Frequent access may be difficult to reconcile with preserving the book for future readers.

paraphrases.source: The collector might agree to make the item available for occasional supervised examination, provided that the practical conditions required for protecting it can be established.
paraphrases.rewrite: The collector might permit supervised access if suitable safeguards can be established.

paraphrases.source: A meaningful public purpose does not by itself eliminate the practical costs of caring for an object or justify ignoring the interests of the people who contribute to its preservation.
paraphrases.rewrite: A worthy public goal alone cannot remove preservation costs or justify ignoring contributors' interests.
